cause_fixed: The SVD describes one peripheral with a single address block whose size spans a range that includes another peripheral's address (POK). The peripheral has two separate register banks with a gap between them, so one contiguous block spans the other peripheral's range.
fix_fixed: Split the peripheral into two SVD peripherals, one per register bank, each with its own baseAddress and a small addressBlock covering only its own range (for example ASG-low at 0x50097000 and ASG-high at 0x58010000, both with groupName ASG, each with a 0x1000 size block). The thread offers this split as a suggestion; it does not confirm the warning is gone.

cause_fixed: GDB 14.2, 15.2, 16.3, 17.1 and 17.2 print thread IDs above 0x7fffffff as signed 32-bit integers and send them back in negative hexadecimal form. pyOCD then appears unable to match the selector to the RTOS thread, leaving the target stopped at the breakpoint. This occurs when RTOS RAM is at or above 0x80000000.
fix_fixed: Use a pyOCD build that includes pull request 2052; the reporter tested this change on the IMXRT1050-EVK and confirmed that Continue resumed. The thread suggests handling the negative selector by recovering the original positive 32-bit ID, keeping special selectors 0 and -1.
versions_fixed: Affected: GDB 14.2, 15.2, 16.3, 17.1, 17.2. Not affected: GDB 18.1. No pyOCD release is named; the fix is pyOCD PR 2052.

cause_fixed: With --rebuild, cbuild cleaned every context of the project rather than only the contexts selected by the active target set. Output directories of another target type that the active target consumes as external inputs were therefore deleted, so the build failed. A separate misconfiguration in the example project (a target-set pointing at the wrong project-context) caused a related wrong selection in the original CI run.
fix_fixed: Upgrade to a cbuild build that includes the fix from PR 684, which the thread gives as the fix for this issue. Nightly build 2026-10-09 was validated with a normal --active AVH-NS-only@Debug build; the thread does not confirm the --rebuild case. Also check that each target-set references the project-context matching its set name.
versions_fixed: Reported with CMSIS-Toolbox cbuild 2.14.x; fix validated on nightly build 2026-10-09 (PR 684).

problems: The thread names no pyOCD release. Comment 4 only says 'pyOCD now behaves similar as uVision', so 'update to a pyOCD release' and 'fixed-in-release' go beyond the thread.
The cause is only implied. The thread shows that uVision moves the PC past the BKPT and that the pyOCD behaviour is to be fixed in pyocd, but it does not give the mechanism as stated.
cause_fixed: A BKPT instruction written into the source halts the core, and pyOCD did not advance the program counter past it, so resuming re-triggered the same breakpoint and Step left the PC unchanged. uVision advances the PC to the next instruction.
fix_fixed: pyOCD was changed so that Step steps over the BKPT instruction and Continue runs past it, behaving similarly to uVision.

cause_fixed: The last (Notes) column used different minimum-width behavior for the header and the data rows. Shrinking it made the data cells keep narrowing while the header stopped, so their right edges no longer lined up. The data rows also did not extend to the viewport edge when the combined column widths were smaller than the available space.
fix_fixed: The thread reports validation on CMSIS Debugger build 1.9.1-9-gda28d9a and closes the issue; it describes no code change, so use that build and do not assume a specific patch.

The thread shows the failure reproduced by lowering the timeout to 100-500 ms, not that the default is confirmed too short for this machine.
cause_fixed: The pyOCD GDB server appears to be forcefully terminated during disconnect before it finishes. The thread suspects the CDT GDB Adapter's server disconnect timeout is too short on slower machines, and that some disconnect problem specific to this board may also be involved. The thread does not explain why the next launch fails with 'PC register is not available'.
fix_fixed: Increase serverDisconnectTimeout in the launch configuration's target section, for example to 3000 ms. This is the initial workaround; a managed-launch-configuration change to set a higher timeout is in progress (#1293). Using the manual RESET button or power-cycling the board restores debugging in the meantime.

problems: Digest says the fix is 'fixed in pyocd 0.45.2.dev39+ga3e58b2b5', but the thread only shows that build was tested and works in a CMSIS Debugger nightly. It does not say that build is the first release containing the fix.

cause_fixed: Trace setup is generated only for features that are enabled, so a feature switched off in the session emits no register write that could clear its enable bit. pyOCD then programs registers by read-modify-write from the enabled features only, so the previously set bits stay on in the target.
fix_fixed: The trace specification was extended so that cleared or reset register states for disabled features are also sent to pyOCD, which applies them. pyTS and pyOCD were updated to support this. Tested with pyocd 0.45.2.dev39+ga3e58b2b5 in CMSIS Debugger Nightly 1.8.1-78-g8c7d39f, where disabled trace features such as exception trace were reported to work as expected.
versions_fixed: Tested with pyocd 0.45.2.dev39+ga3e58b2b5 in CMSIS Debugger Nightly 1.8.1-78-g8c7d39f

cause_fixed: VS Code asks the debug adapter to evaluate Watch and hover expressions before any stack frame exists. The CDT GDB Adapter requires a frame ID for evaluation, so it rejects these early requests. This is a timing race inside the GDB adapter, not a firmware or CMSIS Debugger fault.
fix_fixed: The popups can usually be ignored; the debugger still stops correctly in main(). The race is a known issue in the CDT GDB Adapter (related to #862) and was rescheduled to CMSIS Debugger 1.12.0. The thread is still open and no fix has landed.
versions_fixed: Seen in CMSIS Debugger 1.9.0; rescheduled target 1.12.0

problems: Cause states as fact that the spec 'has no way' to tell the reset sequence whether to halt; the thread only says an update 'may' be needed to pass more context.
Fix claims the pack's debug sequences can then be updated; the thread does not state this step.
Resolution 'workaround' is stated while the issue is still open and no fix is released; the thread only shows sysresetreq working in the example projects.
cause_fixed: Debug sequences currently always halt the device after a reset, even when the user only wants the application to run. For some boards, a manual pyOCD run with the default or other reset methods can stop at an unexpected address, while reset_type=sysresetreq avoids the problem. A debug sequences specification update allowing the reset to be told whether the CPU should halt or keep running may be needed.
fix_fixed: For affected boards, run pyOCD with -O reset_type=sysresetreq as a workaround. The proper fix needs a debug description spec update (Open-CMSIS-Pack-Spec PR 419) and pyOCD support expected in 1.10.0; the thread notes this only helps after release.
versions_fixed: pyOCD 1.10.0 (expected; not yet released at the time of the thread)

cause_fixed: When a node in the Configuration Wizard graphical view is selected, the source editor is synced to that node's annotation location. This sync keeps running while the user edits in source mode, so pauses in typing or saving move the scroll position and cursor back to the selected node's annotation.
fix_fixed: Workaround: close the graphical view until the edits in the source view are done. The maintainer's expectation is that the cursor sync from the graphical view ends once the user moves the cursor or clicks into the source editor. Nightly build 2026-10-11 was validated as no longer showing the jumps, and nightly 1.72.1-24-20261012 was confirmed.

Versions line says 0.44.1 and 0.45.1 as reported; the thread reports 0.44.1 and only says 0.45.1 was inspected and the logic appears unchanged.
cause_fixed: When the FLM sector range covers the whole parent memory region, pyOCD creates no subregions and never copies the FLM valEmpty value to the parent flash region's erased_byte_value. The region keeps the default 0xFF, so the flash builder pads sparse image holes with 0xFF even though the device erases to 0x00.
fix_fixed: The thread points to PR #2032, which propagates FlashDevice.valEmpty to the parent FlashRegion.erased_byte_value; the thread does not name a release containing it. Until a release includes the fix, a project-local pyocd_user.py hook can set erased_byte_value to 0x00 on the flash region.

problems: Cause mechanism is inferred: the thread says device info in target-type makes processor names available, but not that the extension 'could not list the cores' as the digest states.
Resolution 'fixed-in-release' is not shown: the thread is closed and comment 5 says the fix was made, but it names no release, version or PR.

Fix wording presents the target-type device entry as the fix; comment 2 only reports it makes start-pname selectable, and the thread's real change is reading processor names from generated *.cbuild.yml files.
cause_fixed: The start processor of a multi-core device is chosen from the order of the project entries. Processor names are known only when the device is given in the target-type of the csolution file; when the device is set only in the cproject file, start-pname could not be picked in Manage Solution.
fix_fixed: Add the device to the target-type in the csolution file, for example under the target-type's device key, so the processor names are known and start-pname can be selected. As a workaround, add start-pname under the debugger node by hand. The extension now fetches device and processor names from the generated *.cbuild.yml files, so the same selection works when only the board is given in the target-type.

cause_fixed: csolution loads installed packs rather than only those selected by the active solution. The RTE kernel's LoadAndInsertPacks returns immediately when loading one pack fails, so a malformed installed PDSC produces an error even for solutions that do not need that pack. The reporter guesses this is the cause.

cause_fixed: When pyocd commander cannot find the probe given by unique ID, it prints the error but exits with status 0 instead of a non-zero code, so scripts that check the return code see success.
fix_fixed: A maintainer says the problem should be fixed with PR #2037; the issue is still open and the thread gives no interim workaround.

problems: Attributes the proposal to 'the maintainer'; the thread (Comment 1) does not identify the commenter as a maintainer.
States the PR as 'proposed' while the thread says #2061 implements the workaround; the thread does not say whether it is merged or confirmed.
cause_fixed: When a CMSIS-DAP reply is exactly the packet size (512 bytes), the probe ends the bulk IN transfer with a zero-length packet. pyOCD reads one USB packet per command, so it takes that empty packet as the reply to the next command. The real reply is then left unread in the probe, and every later command times out.
fix_fixed: In the PyUSBv2 receive task, read again whenever a read returns zero bytes, and only pass non-empty data on to the reply queue, since no valid CMSIS-DAP reply is empty. Pull request #2061 implements this workaround; the thread says the probe should not send the zero-length packet, so the probe-side behaviour is the underlying defect.
versions_fixed: pyOCD 0.45.1 on Windows 10 with a Microchip PICkit Basic running CMSIS-DAP v2 firmware; the fix is in PR #2061 and the thread does not show a release.
